p: Marine Parade is right on Barmouth's seafront, so Funland is perfectly placed for a quick go on the machines between paddles on the beach. The town is squeezed between the sea and a steep hillside, and it's well worth a climb above the rooftops.

Dinas Oleu, the hillside above the town, was the very first piece of land given to the National Trust, back in 1895, and the views over Cardigan Bay are cracking. Down by the harbour, you can watch the boats come and go, and the little ferry across the river mouth to Fairbourne runs in season. Trains on the Cambrian Coast line stop in town, so it's easy to visit car-free.
